title: Additive comparison of epimorphic augmentation cone families
statement: Let C and D be abelian categories and E:C -> D an additive functor. Let K_n, L_n be integer cochain complexes, f_n:K_n -> L_n, and t_nm:K_m -> K_n, q_nm:L_m -> L_n supplied for every n<=m, with t_nm f_n = f_m q_nm. Let epsilon:T -> Q be a morphism of strict inverse towers of D-complexes. Supply level isomorphisms eK_n:E(K_n) -> T_n and eQ_n:E(L_n) -> Q_n identifying each E(f_n) with epsilon_n, and suppose eK intertwines every t_nm. If each E(f_n) is epimorphic, the target comparisons also intertwine every q_nm. Consequently the images of the homotopy cofibers of f_n are isomorphic, naturally for every n<=m and the given strict square maps, to the actual levels of the mapping cone of the transposed tower morphism epsilon. No Koszul, sheaf, scalar or exactness hypothesis is used.

source.place: Section Cones and termwise split sequences, definition-cone (014E) and lemma-functorial-cone (014F); Mathlib mappingCone.mapHomologicalComplexIso and mappingCone.map_comp.

proof.text: Cancel E(f_m) in each strict transition square, using its epimorphy, the augmentation identifications, eK naturality and epsilon naturality. This proves eQ naturality.

Use the additive cone comparison and the cone isomorphism of the source and target level isomorphisms. The additive cone comparison is natural: check the two cone summand inclusions, whose sum of projections is the identity. Composition of cone maps proves naturality under the strict squares. A direct computation identifies homotopyCofiber.mapArrowHom with mappingCone.map.

Use only the proved private levelConeTowerIso helper of FlatConstantTensorProZeroCones to identify levelwise cones with evaluation of the cone of the transposed tower. Its naturality finishes the stated comparison. No pro-zero result is used.

theorem additiveConeFamilyComparison
    {C D : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] [Abelian C] [Abelian D]
    (E : C ⥤ D) [E.Additive]
    (K L : ℕ → CochainComplex C ℤ) (f : ∀ n, K n ⟶ L n)
    (t : ∀ n m : ℕ, n ≤ m → (K m ⟶ K n))
    (q : ∀ n m : ℕ, n ≤ m → (L m ⟶ L n))
    (hc : ∀ n m h, t n m h ≫ f n = f m ≫ q n m h)
    {T Q : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex D ℤ} (ε : T ⟶ Q)
    (eK : ∀ n, (E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (K n) ≅ T.obj (op n))
    (eQ : ∀ n, (E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (L n) ≅ Q.obj (op n))
    (haug : ∀ n, (E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map (f n) ≫ (eQ n).hom =
      (eK n).hom ≫ ε.app (op n))
    (ht : ∀ n m h, (E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map (t n m h) ≫ (eK n).hom =
      (eK m).hom ≫ T.map (homOfLE h).op)
    (hfepi : ∀ n, Epi ((E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map (f n))) :
    ∃ e : ∀ n, (E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        (HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber (f n)) ≅
      (CochainComplex.mappingCone
        ((HomologicalComplex.functorEquivalence D (.up ℤ) ℕᵒᵖ).inverse.map ε)).asFunctor.obj
          (op n),
      ∀ n m h, (E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map
          (HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber.mapArrowHom (f m) (f n)
            (fun j : ℤ ↦ ⟨j - 1, sub_add_cancel j 1⟩)
            (Arrow.homMk (t n m h) (q n m h) (hc n m h))) ≫ (e n).hom =
        (e m).hom ≫ (CochainComplex.mappingCone
          ((HomologicalComplex.functorEquivalence D (.up ℤ) ℕᵒᵖ).inverse.map ε)).asFunctor.map
            (homOfLE h).op
